dedupe_keys.name: privacy rights clearinghouse data breach chronology

description: The Data Breach Chronology compiles publicly reported data breach notifications from US government agencies into one searchable database, with breach type, affected organisation, compromised information and reporting timelines. The page cites more than 75,000 reported breaches since 2005 and, elsewhere, nearly 100,000. It is maintained by Privacy Rights Clearinghouse, a consumer privacy organisation, with the current version developed by its associate director of policy. Coverage is the United States, from notifications made to federal and state agencies, whose reporting rules differ. Search by organisation, breach type, state or data source and interactive visualisations are free online, and the full database is available by purchase or annual subscription with monthly updates, offered as SQLite, Excel or CSV, with free samples, a README and academic discounts. Caveats: it relies on public notifications, so it is not a complete or verified list, and the provider makes no representation of accuracy. For simulation it gives event histories of breaches by sector for estimating the frequency of cyber incidents that hit banks, insurers and other services, as inputs to resilience studies. It is related to the CISSM Cyber Events Database and HHS health data breach portal records in this catalogue.
